userPrompt: What is the hardest natural substance?
responseText:
**Diamond** is the hardest natural substance.

It ranks 10 on the Mohs scale and has the highest Vickers hardness (~100-150 GPa) of any material that occurs naturally. Its exceptional hardness comes from the rigid, three-dimensional tetrahedral lattice of carbon atoms bonded by strong covalent bonds.

No other naturally occurring material comes close. (Note: lab-made materials like aggregated diamond nanorods or some exotic carbon allotropes can be harder, but they are not natural.)
